column1: The conviction that historical relics provide infallible testimony about the past is rooted in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, when science was regarded as objective and value free.
column2: 人们坚信历史遗物能提供绝对可靠的过去证据，这一信念源于19世纪至20世纪初，当时科学被视为客观且无偏见的。

column1: As one writer observes: ‘Although it is now evident that artefacts are as easily altered as chronicles, public faith in their veracity endures: a tangible relic seems ipso facto real.’
column2: 正如一位作者所说：“如今人们已经清楚，文物和编年史一样容易被改动，但公众依然相信文物真实无伪。遗物是有形的，单凭这一点，人们就觉得它是真的。”
column6: as easily altered as|与……一样容易被改动
column12: ipso facto|adv. 单凭这一事实

column1: Such conviction was, until recently, reflected in museum displays.
column2: 直到最近，博物馆的展品仍然体现了这种信念。

column1: Museums used to look - and some still do - much like storage rooms of objects packed together in showcases: good for scholars who wanted to study the subtle differences in design, but not for the ordinary visitor, to whom it all looked alike.
column2: 过去的博物馆很像储藏室，各种物件挤在陈列柜里，有些博物馆至今还是这样。这种布置适合想研究设计细微差别的学者，却不适合普通参观者。在他们看来，这些东西都差不多。

column1: Similarly, the information accompanying the objects often made little sense to the lay visitor.
column2: 同样，那些与物体相关的信息往往对普通参观者来说并没有什么实际意义。

column1: The content and format of explanations dated back to a time when the museum was the exclusive domain of the scientific researcher.
column2: 这些讲解的内容与形式，都源自于博物馆还是科研人员专属领域的时代。

column1: Recently, however, attitudes towards history and the way it should be presented have altered.
column2: 然而，最近人们对历史及其呈现方式的态度已经发生了变化。

column1: The key word in heritage display is now ‘experience’, the more exciting the better and, if possible, involving all the senses.
column2: 在遗产展示中，关键词是‘体验’，越有刺激性越好，如果可能，应让所有感官都参与其中。
column10: involving|让所有感官都参与其中

column1: Good examples of this approach in the UK are the Jorvik Centre in York; the National Museum of Photography, Film and Television in Bradford; and the Imperial War Museum in London.
column2: 在英国，这种做法的典型代表有约克的约克维克中心、布拉德福德的摄影、电影与电视国家博物馆，以及伦敦的帝国战争博物馆。

column1: In the US the trend emerged much earlier: Williamsburg has been a prototype for many heritage developments in other parts of the world.
column2: 在美国，这一趋势出现得更早：威廉斯堡成为全球许多遗产开发项目的原型。

column1: No one can predict where the process will end.
column2: 没有人能够预测这个过程最终会走向何方。

column1: On so-called heritage sites the re-enactment of historical events is increasingly popular, and computers will soon provide virtual reality experiences, which will present visitors with a vivid image of the period of their choice, in which they themselves can act as if part of the historical environment.
column2: 在所谓的历史遗址，历史事件重演越来越受欢迎。计算机也将很快提供虚拟现实体验，让游客生动地看到自己选择的历史时期，仿佛置身当时的环境，亲自参与其中。
column11: period of their choice|自己选择的时期

column1: Such developments have been criticised as an intolerable vulgarisation, but the success of many historical theme parks and similar locations suggests that the majority of the public does not share this opinion.
column2: 这些发展曾被批评是无法忍受的庸俗化，但许多历史主题公园及类似场所的成功表明，公众多数并不持有这种观点。

column1: In a related development, the sharp distinction between museum and heritage sites on the one hand, and theme parks on the other, is gradually evaporating.
column2: 与此相关的另一个变化是，博物馆和历史遗址与主题公园之间原本鲜明的界线，正在逐渐消失。
column6: on the one hand|指比较中的一方
column8: on the other|指比较中的另一方

column1: They already borrow ideas and concepts from one another.
column2: 它们已经从彼此那里借鉴了许多想法和概念了。

column1: For example, museums have adopted story lines for exhibitions, sites have accepted ‘theming’ as a relevant tool, and theme parks are moving towards more authenticity and research-based presentations.
column2: 例如，博物馆开始用故事线索串联展览，历史遗址也认可围绕主题来组织展示的做法，而主题公园则越来越重视真实性，并以研究为依据来安排展示。
column7: theming|n. 围绕主题组织展示

column1: In zoos, animals are no longer kept in cages, but in great spaces, either in the open air or in enormous greenhouses, such as the jungle and desert environments in Burgers’ Zoo in Holland.
column2: 在动物园里，动物已不再关在笼中，而是养在宽阔的空间里，有的在露天，有的在巨大的温室里。荷兰伯格斯动物园内的丛林和沙漠环境便是例子。

column1: This particular trend is regarded as one of the major developments in the presentation of natural history in the twentieth century.
column2: 这一趋势被视为20世纪自然历史展示领域中的重大发展之一。

column1: Theme parks are undergoing other changes, too, as they try to present more serious social and cultural issues, and move away from fantasy.
column2: 主题公园也在发生其他变化，试图呈现更严肃的社会与文化问题，摆脱幻想。

column1: This development is a response to market forces and, although museums and heritage sites have a special, rather distinct role to fulfil, they are also operating in a very competitive environment, where visitors make choices on how and where to spend their free time.
column2: 这一发展是对市场力量的响应。虽然博物馆和文化遗产场所扮演着特殊的、独特的角色，但它们也处于一个竞争非常激烈的环境中——游客们会自行决定如何以及在哪里度过他们的空闲时间。

column1: Heritage and museum experts do not have to invent stories and recreate historical environments to attract their visitors: their assets are already in place.
column2: 遗产和博物馆专家无需编造故事或重现历史场景来吸引游客——他们的资产早已存在，无需再花费精力去创造新的体验。

column1: However, exhibits must be both based on artefacts and facts as we know them, and attractively presented.
column2: 然而，展品必须基于真实文物和事实，并以引人注目的方式呈现。

column1: Those who are professionally engaged in the art of interpreting history are thus in a difficult position, as they must steer a narrow course between the demands of ‘evidence’ and ‘attractiveness’ especially given the increasing need in the heritage industry for income-generating activities.
column2: 因此，专门从事历史解读的人处境艰难。他们必须在“证据”和“吸引力”两方面的要求之间谨慎权衡，尤其是考虑到文化遗产行业越来越需要能够创收的活动。
column6: in a difficult position|处境艰难
column7: steer a narrow course|在限制中谨慎权衡

column1: It could be claimed that in order to make everything in heritage more ‘real’, historical accuracy must be increasingly altered.
column2: 可以说，为了使所有与遗产相关的元素都显得更加‘真实’，历史准确性就必须被不断修正。

column1: For example, Pithecanthropus erectus is depicted in an Indonesian museum with Malay facial features, because this corresponds to public perceptions.
column2: 例如，直立人这一物种在印度尼西亚的博物馆中被描绘成具有马来族特征，因为这符合公众的认知。

column1: Similarly, in the Museum of Natural History in Washington, Neanderthal man is shown making a dominant gesture to his wife.
column2: 同样，在华盛顿的自然历史博物馆中，尼安德特人被展示为向妻子做出支配性手势。

column1: Such presentations tell us more about contemporary perceptions of the world than about our ancestors.
column2: 这样的展示更反映的是当代人对世界的看法，而非对祖先的看法。

column1: There is one compensation, however, for the professionals who make these interpretations: if they did not provide the interpretation, visitors would do it for themselves, based on their own ideas, misconceptions and prejudices.
column2: 不过，对于作出这些解读的专业人员来说，有一点可以聊以自慰。如果他们不提供解读，游客也会根据自己的想法、误解和偏见自行解释。

column1: And no matter how exciting the result it would contain a lot more bias than the presentations provided by experts.
column2: 无论结果多么令人兴奋，其中所包含的偏见都会远超专家所提供的介绍。

column1: Human bias is inevitable, but another source of bias in the representation of history has to do with the transitory nature of the materials themselves.
column2: 人类的偏见是不可避免的，但历史呈现中的另一种偏见则源于材料本身的易逝性。

column1: The simple fact is that not everything from history survives the historical process.
column2: 事实上，并非历史上的所有事物都能在历史的进程中得以保留下来。

column1: Castles, palaces and cathedrals have a longer lifespan than the dwellings of ordinary people.
column2: 城堡、宫殿和大教堂的寿命比普通人的住宅要长得多。

column1: The same applies to the furnishings and other contents of the premises.
column2: 同样的规则也适用于场所的家具及其他物品。

column1: In a town like Leyden in Holland, which in the seventeenth century was occupied by approximately the same number of inhabitants as today, people lived within the walled town, an area more than five times smaller than modern Leyden.
column2: 以荷兰莱顿为例，十七世纪时的居民人数与今天大致相同，但当时人们住在城墙以内，那片区域的面积还不到现代莱顿的五分之一。
column8: walled town|城墙围起来的城镇
column10: more than five times smaller than|面积不到……的五分之一

column1: In most of the houses several families lived together in circumstances beyond our imagination.
column2: 在大多数房屋里，几个家庭共同生活，这种情形远超我们的想象。

column1: Yet in museums, fine period rooms give only an image of the lifestyle of the upper class of that era.
column2: 然而，在博物馆中，那些精美的历史房间所展示的，只是那个时代上层阶级生活方式的影像而已。

column1: No wonder that people who stroll around exhibitions are filled with nostalgia; the evidence in museums indicates that life was so much better in the past.
column2: 难怪那些在展览馆里闲逛的人会充满怀旧之情；博物馆中的展品表明，过去的生活确实比现在美好得多。

column1: This notion is induced by the bias in its representation in museums and heritage centres.
column2: 这种观念源于博物馆和文化遗产中心在展示方式上的偏差。
